title: What If Every Police Officer in a City Walked Out for a Day? Montreal Found Out in 1969

scenes.text: What if every police officer in a city walked out at once? Montreal tried it. Sixteen hours.
October 7, 1969. Angry about pay, all 3,800 Montreal police go on strike. 2,400 firefighters join them.
Within hours: seven bank robberies, more than 30 armed holdups, over 450 break-ins. Shop windows smashed and looted.
By evening a taxi drivers' protest turns into a riot. Buses burn. A shoot-out at a garage kills a provincial police officer.
Around 30 people are injured, more than 100 arrested. Damage: about two million dollars, over 14 million today.
That night the province passed an emergency law and called in the army. By midnight the police were back. Sixteen hours was enough.

description:
What if a city's entire police force walked out? On 7 October 1969 about 3,800 Montreal police officers struck over pay, joined by about 2,400 firefighters. In roughly 16 hours the city saw seven bank robberies, more than 30 armed holdups and over 450 break-ins.
A taxi drivers' protest turned into the Murray-Hill riot: vehicles were burned, shops looted, one Quebec provincial police officer was killed, about 30 people were injured and more than 100 arrested, with damage of about 2 million dollars (over 14 million today). The Quebec National Assembly passed an emergency law and the army was sent in; the police returned by midnight.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: The strike worked: Montreal police pay roughly doubled within five years. What should happen if a whole profession stopped for a day? Drop your own what-if below.
